_comment: TEMPLATE ONLY -- contains no credentials.
Copy to /etc/sing-box/config.json on box, fill in the REPLACE_ME values,
then lock it down:
sudo mkdir -p /etc/sing-box
sudo cp files/sing-box/config.template.json /etc/sing-box/config.json
sudo $EDITOR /etc/sing-box/config.json
sudo chown root:root /etc/sing-box/config.json
sudo chmod 0600 /etc/sing-box/config.json
NEVER commit the filled-in version: it holds a trojan password and a
vmess UUID.  It deliberately lives outside /gnu/store, which is
world-readable.

servers._comment: Home mesh: resolves the .lan zone via the Pi4's dnsmasq. REPLACE_ME_PI4_LAN_IP is the Pi4's real LAN address (e.g. 192.168.0.x), not its DDNS hostname -- this query itself only needs to reach the Pi4 once home-out is already up.

rules._comment: Must come before the broader 'outbound: any' rule below -- sing-box evaluates dns.rules top-to-bottom, first match wins, so a .lan rule placed after a rule matching everything would never fire.

_comment: Home mesh outbound -- separate from the Hetzner egress outbounds above.
Dials the Pi4 gateway's hysteria2 inbound, used only for traffic
matched to the home LAN / .lan zone by route.rules below.
This device needs its OWN password here, matching one entry in the
Pi4 server's hysteria2 'users' array -- never reuse another device's
password.  That is what makes a lost/stolen device revocable on its
own: delete just its entry server-side and reload, nothing else
changes.
certificate_public_key_sha256 pins the Pi4's self-signed cert by its
public key hash, which is why server_name below can be an arbitrary
string rather than a real, publicly-issued-cert-bearing hostname --
pinning replaces CA trust entirely for this connection.  Get the
hash with, on the Pi4:
openssl x509 -in <cert.pem> -pubkey -noout |
openssl pkey -pubin -outform der |
openssl dgst -sha256 -binary | base64
Home mesh, for road devices (phone, mintsystem): the home LAN is
192.168.0.0/24.  This rule MUST come before the broader LAN
carve-out below, or it is unreachable dead code -- that carve-out
already matches 192.168.0.0/16, a superset, and first-match-wins.
KNOWN TRADEOFF, read before copying this file to box or reform:
those two hosts sit ON 192.168.0.0/24 already.  With this rule in
place, THEIR OWN local-LAN traffic also detours out through
home-out (Pi4, over the internet, back in) instead of staying on
the physical LAN -- wasteful, and it makes local-LAN reachability
on box/reform depend on the internet and the Pi4 being up, which
it did not before.  If that is not acceptable on a given host,
that host's copy of this file can simply omit this rule (or place
it after the LAN carve-out instead) -- these are hand-copied,
not templated per-host, so the two copies can differ.  Road
devices need this rule; box/reform do not.
Home mesh: the .lan zone, resolved via dns-home above and routed
the same way as the CIDR rule immediately above -- same
before-the-carve-out placement, same box/reform tradeoff applies.

rules._comment: Carve-outs: keep LAN and link-local reachable so SSH from other machines, local DNS and NAS/printer keep working.

Never route the VPN server itself through the tunnel -- that is a routing loop. auto_detect_interface normally handles this; this rule is the explicit belt-and-braces version. Set to the server's IP literal, not its hostname.
Guix substitute servers stay direct so builds do not stall behind the tunnel. Remove these two rules if you want literally everything proxied.
